projects.title: Surplus Share (1st Place @ SHSHacks 2024)
projects.description: Surplus Share is an innovative application designed to bridge the gap between businesses with surplus food and individuals in need. Utilizing an advanced heuristic genetic algorithm, the app optimizes delivery routes for drivers, ensuring swift and efficient food distribution. It also incorporates a sophisticated distribution algorithm, considering various factors such as dietary restrictions to facilitate the most effective allocation of food resources.

projects.title: Stock Predictor
projects.description: I worked with Dr. Fouh over the summer to create a working stock predictor web app with support for 3 stocks, Apple, Tesla, and SPY, although more are easily addable. We used linear regression and neural network models to predict opening prices with 1 year to date information.The app was built with Python and Javascript for the backend, using Node.js to host the server and Axois to communicate between the front and the back. Additionally, React.js was used to build the front end with Inline styling.

projects.title: HealthCoachAI (3rd Place @ SHSHacks2023)
projects.description: HealthCoach was built during the 24-hour SHSHacks2023 as a web app to help beginners start their journey to physical wellness. The app includes many tools such as an AI workout generator, macronutrient tracking, and water logging.This app was built using Python/Flask for the backend server, Firestore NoSQL to store all data, and OpenAI GPT-3 to generate workout plans. Additionally Nuxt was used for the frontend development with TailwindCSS as the styling tool

activity.title: I spent 3 days in SF, and the number of people working on something cool was unreal. This is why, for the Y Combinator AI Growth Hackathon, we built Recco. The idea is simple. You walk into a networking event, and the one person who could literally change your life is somewhere in that room, but you have no idea who they are, so you just walk past them. Recco fixes that. It's a camera-first AI networking assistant for iPhone. Point your phone at the room, and it tells you who's worth talking to and why. You can filter the whole room by voice (say "show me AI founders" and the right people light up). Tap someone, and it writes you an opener based on what they're working on. On the tech side: SwiftUI, Convex backend, ArcFace embeddings for face recognition, Deepgram for voice, and Fiber AI (YC S23) for pulling real identities. Our ideal vision was Meta glasses or a small wearable camera, but we had to ship with photo input due to time constraints. Watch the demo; we spent a long time on it, please. Big thank you to my team, Dat Nguyen , Bryan Pham , and Pranav Sagar . None of this would have been possible without them. Check out the code: https://lnkd.in/gqXswzWX #YCHackathon #AI #Hackathon #SF #ComputerVision #Deepgram ...more

Walked into the Berkeley AI Hackathon without a team... Got “interviewed” by one (mostly to see if I could TikTok dance 😅)… And then we got to work. We built Aside AI, an AI narrator that watches the room and narrates your life out loud. This ended up being my biggest hackathon experience yet: • 2,000+ attendees • 500+ projects • Backed by some incredible sponsors: Special thanks to QNX , Deepgram and Simular In just 24 hours, we didn’t just build we shipped and marketed(@aside_ai): • 20K+ views across our reels • 110+ new followers • 500+ likes We captured our side quests (push-up fades, eating challenges, etc.), build progress, and meetings with potential customers, and met some amazing people like our interns ( Tyler hwang and James Hansen ). We won Best Use of Deepgram and lost the Questionable Use track after. The biggest thing I learned from this hackathon is the power of networking and the power of a like minded team. None of this would have happened if I didn't take the first step and find people that had similar goals to mine. Big thanks to Naomi Carrigan for being their to answer any questions we had for the Deepgram track. Huge shoutout to my team ask well, Bryan Pham , Ethan Nguyen , and Dat Nguyen . Special thanks to Pranay Yalamanchali and Tanay Karumanchi for pulling up for extra support. Hi everyone! Last weekend, I had the opportunity to participate in SAC HACKS! In short, we found that many students who received food from our on-campus food pantry did not know what to do with their ingredients. Our solution: We built an AI-powered recipe generator as our core feature to solve this. Key features included: Ingredient-based matching, Smart filtering for dietary restrictions, allergens, available appliances, and cooking time. An Aggie community page where students can share their own recipes. What I learned: We didn’t place, potentially due to my lack of foresight. I was too quick to jump on a solution instead of exploring border ideas/problems first. I learned from multiple mentors that thinking of "crazy" ideas is the way to grow—start with something big or seemingly impossible in terms of technical ability, then TRY IT! From there, you can scale down. Nonetheless, it was an amazing opportunity, and I am very grateful for my team: Daniel Kagramanov , Annika Gangrade , Theresa Dinh . The demo is below! https://lnkd.in/gA78_v6r ...more

24 Hours. 🥉 3rd Place at ProdCon! I’m excited to share that last weekend, my partner Manraj Thandi and I competed in ProdCon, UC Davis’ annual product development hackathon. As Computer Engineering majors, stepping into the world of product development was both exciting and challenging. From pitching to execution, we faced our share of obstacles, but the experience pushed us to think beyond code and focus on real user problems. We, like many students, know that switching majors is confusing, stressful, and often discouraging. Many don’t know what credits transfer, how long the switch will take, or whether they’ll still be able to graduate on time. Using this insight, we built Dadvisor, a tool designed to help students confidently switch majors while staying on track academically. Our goal was to simplify decision-making and give students clarity when navigating their academic paths. With the help of incredible mentors and organizers, we were proud to place 3rd overall among so many talented teams. Special thanks to Curtis Chen and Samar Varma for their guidance and support. Also a huge thank you to The Organizers : AggieWorks , Product Space and AI Student Collective . The Judges: Nagi SriRanga, Andrew Dunckel , Michael Skinner, MBA, CPM , Shiv Shankar , Amar Saurabh , and Lovlesh Chhabra Excited to learn about product space in the future! 🔗 Check out our project here: https://lnkd.in/gkbmkjGN ...more

I MC'd in front of 800 interns at Amazon 's Ready to Launch event and had a fireside chat with Panos Panay , SVP of Devices, Alexa, and Leo. We talked through his career and even played Kahoot. Two parts of our conversation felt particularly personal. The first was about failure. He said failure isn't something to avoid, it's something to learn from and move past. The second was what it takes to be great at something, not just good. He said humility, curiosity, and the courage to fail fast. Those three things carried him throughout his career. We also disagreed about pizza. He said his favorite topping was cheese. I had to address my concerns that cheese isn't a real topping. Ready to Launch is about celebrating what everyone put into their internship this summer, and getting to host it was something I never expected to do. It was my first time doing anything like this. Panos was kind and made the whole thing easy, and the conversation felt natural, as if we had known each other for years! Thank you to Panos for your time, and to everyone who made this possible.

"Jarvis, I'm struggling to learn gradient descent, can you teach me?" "Pulling up your whiteboard rn" 🤯 Was in SF the past few days... Linked w/ Jonah Daian & the VoiceOS (YC P25) founders at their hackathon, shipped their first edtech integration, and won $1k. Built an interactive whiteboard you can just talk to. A voice agent that teaches, draws diagrams, and works through problems on the board with you, and even understands you draw. This method is way more effective to learn difficult concepts than reading from a textbook imo. Building with VoiceOS made me realize voice is the interface of the future, and the fact that you could make custom integrations in like 30 secs was absolutely INSANE. You can essentially control anything on your computer and fully interact with it without touching the keyboard. Highly recommend installing VoiceOS if you haven't already. Also toured Convex hq w/ Wayne Sutton . Got to demo our projects, meet the team + deep discussion abt future of agents + cool merch 😂
New voices on Wednesday. Heads may well be turned 👀
